html:
SMTO-SKL-0157 — SMTO's GitHub feature only works with github.com

GUID: bbc38b69-950f-539f-b612-191e874941d4
Slug: github-host-unsupported
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • Your saved GitHub account points to a server other than github.com, such as a company GitHub Enterprise server. SMTO's GitHub feature can't connect there, so nothing was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If your account is on github.com, open Parameter Store, select the GitHub account entry, open Value, select Reveal & edit value, set the host back to github.com and select Save. The host was changed to something other than github.com, which is the only server this feature can talk to.
  2. If your repository is on a company GitHub server, ask SMTO to work with it using Git commands in the Shell on your computer instead. Git commands can reach your company server, while SMTO's GitHub feature cannot.

What success looks like

  • When you ask SMTO to check your GitHub connection, it shows your github.com login as verified.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change a company server account's host to github.com; its token won't work there.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • GitHub Account profile validation rejected a host other than github.com; the GitHub skill supports only github.com user PATs.

What this means

  • GitHub profile validation receives a host other than github.com. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • GitHub profile validation receives a host other than github.com.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the actual repository host rather than rewriting it to the public service.

How to fix it

  • parameter_profiles.validate requires host == "github.com"; Enterprise and other hosts are not implemented. Restore host to github.com only if the account really is a github.com account; for other hosts use Git commands through the existing Git Working Context/Shell, and do not remap an Enterprise host to github.com.
  • This adapter supports github.com only. Use the existing Git/Shell context for other hosts; do not remap Enterprise hosts to github.com.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported public GitHub profile or an appropriate existing Git/Shell route targets the intended host.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
